_comment: Canonical storage contract. Hand-written and language-neutral on purpose:
generating it from TypeScript would make TS the source of truth and give us
a second artifact to keep in sync, which is the exact failure mode this file
Each case builds a fresh workspace from `setup`, runs `op`, and asserts
`expect`. Error cases assert an error CLASS, not a message string, so the
two languages can word their errors naturally.
Paths in `setup` are workspace-relative. `outside/` is a sibling directory
created next to the workspace, used for escape cases.

cases.name: reads a file at the workspace root
resolves a relative path against the workspace root, not the cwd
cases._why: B5/B11. The welcome document stores `source: data/sales.csv`. Rust used to reject this outright (no parent component) while Node would have resolved it against the process cwd. Both must now mean the same file.

cases.name: accepts an absolute path inside the workspace
reports a missing file as not-found, never as empty content
cases._why: The dev server used to answer a missing file with 200 + index.html, so a missing note read as a successful page of HTML.

cases.name: refuses an absolute path outside the workspace
refuses a sibling directory sharing the workspace name prefix
cases._why: The whole reason containment is component-aware. A JS startsWith() check admits /x/ws-evil for a workspace at /x/ws; path.relative and Rust's Path::starts_with both reject it.

cases.name: refuses a symlink pointing outside the workspace
writes a new file and reads it back
cases._why: The behaviour WebStorage faked: writeFile was a console.warn that reported success.

cases.name: refuses a write that escapes the workspace
refuses a write through an escaping symlink
lists markdown recursively, sorted, skipping dotdirs and other extensions
lists data files by extension, sorted
listing returns absolute paths
cases._why: Web mode used to return bare filenames while Tauri returned absolute paths, so a document authored on desktop could not resolve in the browser.
